root_cause_summary: Customer-site network/PoE port issue affecting device connectivity and operation. When tested on bench was not able to reproduce the issue. No hardware fault identified.
investigation_details: Customer initially reported that the GRS10H was unable to establish audio and displayed the error message “Temporary problem placing call please try again later.” The customer replaced the device locally in an attempt to resolve the issue. During the on-site follow-up, the replacement device was then found to be unable to obtain an IP address. Once the port issue was addressed on the customer side, the replacement device was able to obtain network connectivity, be configured, and operate successfully. The original returned device was later evaluated in R&D and no fault was reproduced. The unit configured normally and was able to place and receive calls on the bench.
troubleshooting_steps: FCT Logs Attached in the comments. FCT passed for all the hardware tests on this device.

R&D Investigation:

* Reviewed the reported issue on primary GRS10 at 10.23.186.207 after the customer observed the message “Temporary problem placing call, please try again later” when answering calls.
* Confirmed the customer had already verified all RCB ports and did not identify any port-level fault.
* Checked the GRS10 for active alarms, alerts, or other visible fault indications at the time of investigation.
* Attempted to validate the issue condition, but the behavior was not reproducible during review.
* Bench-tested the returned original device in R&D by configuring the unit and verifying successful call placement and call reception.

Investigation from Field Notes and Service Engineering Team: (As per the Salesforce and Conversation with the Field Technician)

* Reviewed field service communication and technician notes from the on-site investigation.
* Verified that after the customer replaced the unit, the replacement device was initially unable to obtain an IP address.
* Confirmed with the field technician that on-site IT and FST investigated the connected port and PoE/network path.
troubleshooting_results: The returned original GRS10H device did not have any fault during the bench testing. It was configured on the ECT Server. Same firmware was used on RCB3 and GRS7 as that of GRS10H. The device was able to be configured and was able to place and receive calls in the lab environment. When the hospital received the new device, it initially could not obtain the IP Address until the network port issue was cleared by the Hospital IT Team. After the port/network condition was corrected, the replacement device was configured and used successfully. These findings do not support a hardware failure of the returned original device.

summary: GRS5 Failed during Network Maintenance.
description: NCMR:  NCMR0446716

* QTY: 3
* GRS5 (PN: P2594NNC2D11)
* Serial Numbers: 

    * 041192LTWIS
    * 041192S2WIS
    * 0282006WWIS
    

Described Field Issue: 

During some regular network maintenance 3 x GRS5 failed and could not be powered on. The customer asserted this is not the first time this has happened and is asking why devices failed. 3 devices have been RMA’d back to understand what failed.

These are the GRS5; 0282006WWIS, 041192S2WIS, 041192LTWIS

1ZH920509025475593 is the tracking number for the RMA.

We have identified that the customer is not participating in LLDP on their POE’s and we have asked that they review their POE port settings but we are not sure if that would contribute to a failed device.
root_cause_summary: Two of the three have a crc error when loading both the kernel and recovery images, which indicates that whatever happened during the network maintenance must have caused a communication outage when these devices were in the middle of an update. The other one is in a crash loop.
investigation_details: Engineering Investigation Start Date: 04-MAY-2026

Hardware engineering Investigation Completion Date: 05-MAY-2026

Device Details:

* GRS5 P/N: P2594NNC2D11
* Refer to description section for device serial numbers.

HW Engineering Investigation Summary:

* The returned GRS5 units were tested to verify power functionality. All devices successfully powered ON without any issues. The operating system (OS) was able to boot; however, none of the units were able to launch or load the Nurse Call application software.
* This behavior indicates that the Nurse Call application loading process has been corrupted or compromised. The units appear to be stuck in a crash loop during application initialization.
* Touchscreen hardware functionality was not verified, as the devices did not progress far enough in the boot sequence to load the application.
* Testing was conducted using a HIB fixture environment. Refer to the attachments for corresponding serial numbers and captured boot-up screen information.
* SW team (Mark R.) will continue investigating for possible SW issues due to the application crashing, which can be due to several different things.
* Observations per device: (See attachment for images)

    * 0282006WWIS - Device powered ON and stayed at the ‘System entering recovery mode’ step. Application failed to load.
    * 041192S2WIS - Device powered ON and continuously kept rebooting to load the Application software. Application failed to load. 
    * 041192LTWIS -Device powered ON and failed to load application.   
        
    

SW Investigation:  
  
Two of the three have a crc error when loading both the kernel and recovery images, which indicates that whatever happened during the network maintenance must have caused a communication outage when these devices were in the middle of an update. The other one is in a crash loop.   
  
Customer had mentioned LLDP may have been implicated.   
Possible scenario:

During download/transfer of the software files the RCB was starved of voltage from its PoE port > The child device depends on the RCB for its source of power, so any power instability upstream causes a transient brown out condition for the device ultimately recieving the data.
troubleshooting_steps: Standard Lost Audio Station troubleshooting transpired without the ability to repair the devices.
troubleshooting_results: Replaced devices with newer GRS7’s.
verification_summary: Most likely a network outage while devices were in process of an update.
rca_review_comments: Inconclusive but potentially caused by network outage

investigation_details: Overall, I did not find any glaring issues in the logs for the “4-West MedSurg Primary Console” or the “UH-4W MedSurg Secondary Console”; all of the calls listed in the syslogs match up with the logs in 3CX. For the Primary console, there were plenty of alerts generated before the audio was reset, however, there is no indication (from the logs) that an attempt was made to open audio with a device; after resetting the audio, there was an audio call to 4-West MedSurg RCB3-4166 port 1 ASBC-A that lasted ten (10) seconds.

Between 1:45am and 3:45am, there were no audio calls to the Primary Console, however, there were six (6) audio calls to Secondary Console. One (1) of those audio calls is listed as “Not Answered” and this is most likely due to the fact that the Secondary Console was trying to open audio with (4-West MedSurg RCB3 4805-4810:2) while audio was already open between two GRS5’s (4-West MedSurg RCB3 4805-4810:2) and (4-West MedSurg RCB3 4839-4840-4802:1); the audio was open for forty-six (46) seconds between the two GRS5’s. It is worth noting that if audio is open between two devices and an attempt to call one of those devices is made, a pop-up should appear saying that the call cannot be completed; this pop-up will disappear from the screen after about twenty (20) seconds. It should also be noted that if a call is placed between two GRS5’s, audio is opened and the call is cancelled, then audio will still stay open until the “Hang-Up” button is pressed.

=== KB Article ===
kb_article_id: 2629730338
title: Lost Primary or Secondary Audio Station
text: ## Problem

---

Used when there is a Lost Primary Audio Station or Lost Secondary Audio Station system alert on the primary console and in the Enterprise Configuration Tool's (ECT) 'Active Calls' section.

- Environment: Nurse Call - All versions
- This KB may require an RCB reboot

## Solution

---

1. Determine the audio station type, serial number and RCB port number by performing the following steps:
    1. On the GRS10 console navigate to Menu → System Alerts.
    2. Highlight the **Lost Audio Station** alert and click the **Show Details** button.
    3. At the bottom of the screen note if the Audio station is a GRS5 *(gas)* or SRS *(sas)*, its serial number and RCB Port number.

         For example:*** iob-0xxxxxxxWIS:gas-0xxxxxxxWIS:1*** - where ***iob-*** is RCB serial, ***gas-*** is GRS5 serial and ***:1*** or ***:2*** represent RCB ports that the audio station is connected to - RS1 or RS2 respectively.  
  
    4. If SRS, skip to **step 6**.  
    5. If GRS5 proceed to the next step.  
  
2. Determine if GRS5 is powered on or off, online or offline by performing the following steps:
    1. [Access the command line interface (CLI) of the parent RCB device](https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CTS/pages/888144057/How+to+connect+to+a+base+device+command+line+interface+CLI) (parent of the lost GRS5).
    2. Once at *iob *command prompt, use *ping* command. If GRS5 is in port 1 use *10.0.0.2* IP address, if in port 2 use *10.0.0.6.*
    3. If ping was unsuccessful, skip to **step 5.**
    4. If ping was successful, the GRS5 is powered on and online; proceed to the next step.  
  
3. Determine if the GRS5 is properly configured and on the correct software version by performing the following steps:
    1. [Access the CLI of the GRS5](https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CTS/pages/907903288/How+to+Access+GRS5+GRS7+Command+Line+Interface+CLI).
    2. Once at the  `gas-xxxxxwis $`command prompt, determine if the serial number in the prompt matches the serial number from **step 1.b**.
        1. If serial numbers are mismatched, make the necessary corrections in ECT.
        2. If they are the same, proceed to the next step.
    3. In the command prompt of the GRS, type ***nnc -v*** and hit enter. Note the application software version of the GRS5.
    4. Open Service Portal or SAMM Tool and determine if GRS5 is on the correct software version with the rest of the devices.
        1. If the software is mismatched, download and apply the correct version to the GRS5.
        2. If the software matches proceed to the next step.  
  
4. [Reboot the GRS5 and the parent RCB](https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CTS/pages/1030848709/How+To+Reboot+a+Base+Device) and wait up to 5 min for the alerts to clear.
    1. If the system alert has cleared, complete the CRM resolution fields using the tables below. If issue persists, engage a senior member of your team for further guidance before escalating.  
    2. If the system alert persists, **replace the GRS5**.  
  
5. If ping was unsuccessful, perform the following steps to determine if the GRS5 is powered off or offline.
    1. Power down the parent RCB and test cabling between RCB and GRS5 and visually inspect both ports for damage.
    2. If cable tests passed and no port damage is seen, temporarily swap RS1 and RS2 ports on the RCB and power on the RCB to determine if power is being delivered to GRS5 on the other port.
        1. If power is being delivered to GRS5 and both RS ports are being used, the RCB has a faulty RS port and it needs to be replaced.
        2. If RS2 port was open, configure the GRS5 for port 2 in ECT and publish configuration.
        3. If GRS5 still does not power on, **replace the GRS5**.  
  
6. SRS’s are not IP addressable so no ping command can be performed from its parent RCB to verify the connectivity. A simple way to confirm connectivity of an SRS is to try a PSoC software download to the SRS in Service Portal or SAMM Tool.
    1. If PSoC download is unsuccessful, skip to **step 8**.
    2. If PSoC download is successful the SRS is powered on and online. Proceed to the next step.  
  
7. In Service Portal or SAMM Tool, determine if SRS is on the correct PSoC software version.
    1. If the software matches, try rebooting the SRS via Room Reset on GRS10 or by [rebooting its parent RCB](https://baxter-international.atlassian.net/wiki/spaces/CTS/pages/1030848709/How+To+Reboot+a+Base+Device).
    2. If none of the above fixes the issue, **replace the SRS**.  
  
8. If PSoC download was unsuccessful, perform the following steps to determine if the the SRS is powered off or offline.
9. If confirmed, complete the CRM resolution fields using the table below. If issue persists, engage a senior member of your team for further guidance before escalating.

## Cause

---

Misconfigured device  
Mismatched software versions  
Faulty cabling  
Faulty RCB RS port  
Faulty device

root_cause_summary: The issue was caused by a firmware defect in the Gen 3 PoE switch software that allowed BPDU/STP packets to be transmitted during switch initialization, even when spanning tree had been explicitly disabled on the uplink port using the no spanning-tree configuration. As a result, customer switches configured with BPDU Guard interpreted the unexpected STP traffic as a loop-protection event and automatically disabled the connected uplink port.
investigation_details: See comments
troubleshooting_steps: Reboot PoE switch that is configured with spanning-tree disabled on port 25
troubleshooting_results: Cisco switch will shut uplink port.
rca_review_comments: _We observed that STP packets are transmitted during switch initialization._

_This issue has been logged in our Bugzilla under issue #25664._

_When the command "no spanning-tree" is applied to a port, it is intended to disable the STP function on that port completely, which means that the port should neither transmit nor receive STP packets._

_Based on our test results, the current behavior indicates that the STP mechanism is not properly handled by the software during switch initialization._

root_cause_summary: Customer running monitoring tool that was dragging down the disk reads for sql server.
investigation_details: So we are going to need some help from the customer on this. I hav e attached several screenshots to this ticket as evidence for the customer. The service logs indicate we are getting time outs. When I checked the database server I found IO latency in the SQL Server logs and also a bunch of errors in the event viewer logs. So I checked to make sure the db server was setup correctly to rule out possible bottles necks as recommended by Microsoft.   
The data and log file for the databases are on drives  
Memory settings are set appropriately   
Tempdb files have been created one per core  
Tempdb file size has been set to equal amounts.  
Further research indicated this error can be caused by a few things which is where we need to get the customer db and network people to resolve the initial issues. Microsoft mentioned that SQL Server could be spawning more requests than the IO could handle. The recommendation was to check the IO subsystem driver configuration for a possible misconfiguration.   
Also looking at dm_io_virtual_file_stats the msdb and tempdb have high IO latency. I looked the backups and it seems that all the log files are running at the same time which is hammering write latency for the msdb database. Microsoft recommends staggering the database backups so they are not running all together but one after the other.  
Looking into the dm_db_session_space_usage view I found that there is an external monitoring process that is hammering the tempdb that is causing the IO latency. Its called “SQLExternalMonitoring” This process is creating almost 50GB in the Tempdb and creating excessive disk IO issues.  
This is probably why we are getting timeouts when updating the calls for rounding. We need the customer to stagger the backups and to turn off their monitoring tool. I have included screenshots in the attachment  section for reference. Please let me know if you have any questions.  
Additional info:  
The tempdb is being beat up by   
Azure SQL IaaS monitoring (SqlServerExtension.Service.exe) it is maintaining long-lived shared-memory sessions that are heavily allocating TempDB. It has had an open connection since “2025-11-02 00:32:10.430“. See screenshot.

root_cause_summary: The majority of the issues of the reminder service not working / reminder button presses unresponsive were caused by:  
1) Uncaught exceptions on action blocks  
2) The grs-5 getting out of synchronization with the reminder service.  This would cause the grs-5 to send a completion message when the reminder was on hold.  The reminder service ignored this message.  
Fixes for these issues plus other corner cases were implemented.
investigation_details: We are able to reproduce several reminders defects in the lab - mostly reminders timing out - no longer responding to button pushes on the GRS-5.

We found multiple software defects in the reminder service and reminders gateway plugin:  
1.The gateway plugin was sending back to back reminder completion and reminder running messages to the grs-5's.  If the order of these messages got swapped, it caused a non responsive reminder icon. We eliminated the completion message in this case to eliminate the race.  
2.We added a try / catch / error log around all reminders processing occurring on action blocks.  Some processing was already protected but not all.  This is the cause of sites where reminders as a whole feature is no longer working until the reminder service is restarted.  
3.We eliminated the restart of elapsed on demand timers on reminder service restart.  This eliminated non-starting on demand reminders.  
4.We fixed cases of out of order message completion from the grs-5's.  If the reminder service receives a completion message when the reminder is on hold, it will now treat the message as an off-hold message instead of discarding it.  
5.We fixed a null reference exception that could kill an action block.  
6.We increased the maximum message received size for staff movement and location events.  
7.David G. corrected the scheduler type.  
8.We fixed code that was firing extremely rapid, repetitive sql statements.  
9.We fixed a bug in the reminders editing screen that could leave reminders in an incorrect state.

comment_summary: Rounding reminders were displaying as overdue on Status Board even after being reset, and refreshing Status Board did not correct the customer's case. Websocket captures showed reminder state change, hold change and completion messages arriving out of order through pubsub, revealing a race condition between the state change and hold change messages, and database task instance history initially appeared to show two interleaved task instances until a re-query ordered by insertion id showed the ordering artifact came from identical timestamps. The thread concludes the fault was in the pubsub layer, which was removed from Nurse Call in version 4.1.00 and higher in favour of RabbitMQ messaging.

comment_summary: A Duress Alert placed from a Linq badge appears to be sent twice in rapid succession. Analysis of the logs shows two Duress events arriving roughly 75ms apart for the same location, with the Locating Service logs lacking detail and the Message Service logs showing a CallID of 0 on the second event, suggesting the second Duress published over RabbitMQ was associated with a database INSERT failure that did not stop delivery because of behavior added years ago after a transaction log overflow stopped PubSub processing. The thread reasons that the second Duress likely arrived while the first was still being processed, preventing the duplicate-detection logic from catching it, and notes that Messaging Service determines alert uniqueness from the CallID rather than the CallGuid, so two different CallIDs were treated as two different notifications. A further Duress test was captured with the HillRom.LocatingServiceHost log set to trace, and the thread raises a possible relationship to a more extreme case at another site covered by a separate defect.

description: I logged in to the customer site, bumped up the message service log and watched for calls.

 The VoIP service configuration shows as per Config.jpg: Which is as expected.

This means that the alias we send should start with a 7 and the extension should be only 5 digits in length with a lifetime of 60 minutes.

 Unfortunately because a code change is needed we will need to Nurse Call hotfix this or put it in the next release.

summary: NC - Freeswitch - Avaya Callback not working - Inconsistent extension length
description: In the code, the  root cause issue relates tot he interpretation of ‘Length’ in the appsettings.json file.  One place in the code interprets the length as the prefix+digits.  The other is just digits.  The prefix+digits interpretation is the correct one as the Length was intended to represent the full length of the alias including the prefix.

To force alignment, a single line in the VoIP Service code needs to be amended.  Basically, it is a change to **line 16 of EndpointAliasManager.cs** to read as follows:

```
Limit = (int)Math.Pow(10, length-1);
```

The current implementation for ‘Limit' utilizes the full length.  If the ‘length’ is used instead of ‘length-1’, the ‘Limit’ is calculated as 100000 instead of 10000.  The 'Limit’ value is later used in the code to calculate a modulus of a counter as LastValue%Limit for the alias.  With the current implementation and a Length of 5, the modulus doesn’t revert back to 0 until 999999 is reached.  prefix+digits would result in a value like 799999 (6 digits).

One might think, then, that it would be as simple as just using a Length of 4 rather than 5.  The problem with that thought process relates to how the alias is padded with zeros.  If the LastValue is 1 and the Length is 5, we want an alias of 70001.  If Length is changed to 4, we get a value like 7001 which is wrong.
impact_description: Impact Assessment Summary:  
Due to a calculation error, the alias values for wireless notifications were allowed to exceed the range from 70000-79999.  Instead of rolling back to 0000 after 9999, the code was letting 9999 to go to 10000 and continue to 99999 before rolling back to 0000.    
The fix involves adding unit tests to ensure that the Length (5 characters) is maintained when iterating through the full collection of possible alias extension values + 1.  In other words, the 10000th aliased extension must be 70000 rather than 710000.  
The Unit Test is located in the zep-voip GitHub repo (Voip Service) in Test.Voip->TestVoipAlias.cs->TestVoipAliasRollover().  The test does the following:

* Loop through 10000 alias values
* Ensure that the generated alias value matches the expected length (5 characters)
* Ensure that the alias prefix (7) is the first character of ever alias
* Ensure the first alias after the rollover is zero.

Configuration Service - file ConfigurationService/DataAccess/Device/DeviceDal.cs - in method Delete(), before deleting a voip extension  
from the Extension Manager Database, check to see if the voip extension is still in use in the NavicareEnterprise database.  
If the voip extension is still assigned, do not delete it from the Extension Manager database.   This keeps the two databases in synch  
and prevents duplicate voip extensions from being issued.  
Before: duplicate voip extensions are issued.  
After: No duplicate voip extensions are issued.

steps_taken: 1\. Create 4 new rooms, each with a grs7, do not assign serial numbers to the devices, do not use similar rooms feature yet.  
2\. Create primary console that is also the nursing unit controller for the nursing unit and save.  
3\. Add serial numbers to rcb3 devices and grs10h device and save.    
4\.  Add serial numbers to the grs7 devices and save.

Note: a query can be run against the table asterisk.ps_endpoints in the HRCWSExtensionManager database  (select \* from asterisk.ps_endpoints) at this point in the reproduction to verify the issue is occuring.  The ps_endpoints table will have 0 rows.  It should have a row for each voip extension in use in the navicare database  (select \* from v_voipextensions).

5\. Right click room 4, select create similar rooms.  Make 4 new rooms but do not serialize. click save.

Update July 9, 2024 - It is not necessary to use the create similar rooms feature to reproduce this issue.  The issue is reproduced when rcb(3) boards are saved without a serial number.  If these boards are created manually, one at a time, without using create similar rooms, the issue still occurs.  
Also, if 8 actual or simulated devices are not available as were used in the reproduction steps , fewer devices may be used.  
The issue occurs when unserialized devices are saved, then those devices are given a serial number, and saved, then more devices are added after the second save.

investigation_details: **Why does a Disconnected Switch call get placed?**  The room is configured in ECT but physically not connected

**Why is the switch not physically connected?** Staging the environment, therefore the configured switch needs to be disabled.

**Why does the configured switch need to be disabled?** In order to get rid of the 'disconnected switch' call that is alarming 

 

Scenario:

 

1. You have a room configured in ECT with a bath switch configured but not connected.
2. To stop the bath switch from alarming you disable the bath switch in ECT.
3. With the switch still disconnected, when you enable it in ECT, you don’t get a Disconnected Switch alert.
4. You have to delete the switch, save the configuration and then add the switch back in, and only then you will get a Disconnect Switch alert.

Expectations: the 'disconnect switch' call should display in required places (active calls list in ECT, Staff Console etc.) when the configured switch is re-enabled and not physically connected.

 

We believe that this is a defect against an existing product requirement.
